verdict.rationale: Firecrawl's own docs and README say it returns clean, LLM-ready markdown or structured JSON from any URL. They also claim it handles JS-heavy pages with 'no proxy headaches,' which covers the rendering and blocking parts of the story. One community comment says the open-source and 'Simple' variants lack a proxy service, but that targets self-hosted forks rather than giving a concrete hands-on failure, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of output cleanliness and anti-blocking success, and detailed first-party documentation of how blocking and rendering are handled beyond marketing-level claims.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can get clean LLM-ready text directly instead of dealing with blocking, rendering, and messy HTML myself
